sentences.text: I.A.Nos.25340/2024, 5316/2025, 5317/2025, 23718/2024, 7443/2024, 13166/2025 and 15017/2025 which are applications for urgent hearing, are considered and allowed.
Heard on admission.
Appeal being arguable is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A.No.8033/2024, an application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

2. The appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 7, 8, 13(1)(d)/13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act and sentenced to suffer three years RI with fine of Rs.2000/-,
three years RI with fine of Rs.2000/- and four years RI with fine of Rs.2000/-, with default stipulations.
3. Brief facts of the case are that when complainant Dilip Vyas met with Naib Tahsildar Raveesh Singh Bhadauria then he told him to meet his peon Rajendra Singh.
When complainant met with peon Rajendra Singh then Rajendra Singh demanded Rs.1.00 lac as bribe for the mutation in survey No. 2870 and thereafter get the bribe on 14.07.15.
Accordingly, offence has 2 CRA-3429-2024 been registered.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that trial Court has wrongly convicted the appellant without proper appreciation of facts of the case as well as evidence on record.
The appellant was on bail during trial, but he did not misuse the liberty so granted.
It is further submitted that from the date of judgment i.e. 19.2.2024 he is in custody, thus he has suffered more than one year and six months jail sentence.
There is no likelihood of hearing of the instant appeal in near future.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in both the cases the Supreme Court granted bail to the appellants after they had undergone eight months of custody, considering it sufficient for grant of suspension of sentence.

In the case of Balveer Singh vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 14.3.2023 in Cr.A No.4440 of 2022, ten months of custody was considered sufficient for grant of suspension of sentence to the appellant, who had been convicted under Section 13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for four years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore,
it is prayed that the 3 CRA-3429-2024 remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended.
5.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

Considering the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant, as well as the attending facts and circumstances of the case, the evidence available on record, and the contentions put forth by the counsel, but without commenting on the merits of the case, I.A. is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.

The appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 10/10/2025 and on subsequent dates given by the Registry in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
8. Registry is directed to list the case for final hearing in due course.

C.C. as per Rules (ANIL VERMA) JUDGE (alok)
